processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The two steel compositions (M1 = Fe-8Mn-3Al-0.2C and M2 = Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C) were fabricated using a vacuum arc melting furnace; the melted ingot was remelted 4 times by flipping the ingot before each remelt to ensure complete and uniform melting of raw materials throughout the ingot.
Homogenization of as-cast samples was carried out at 1100 °C for 2 h, followed by water quenching. This homogenized + water-quenched condition is designated M2-HQ (Nomenclature for 3Al-1Si (M2)).

structures.overall_structure: Homogenized + water-quenched M2 microstructure: the optical micrograph (500 µm scale bar) shows a lighter matrix with scattered dark features.

characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural imaging of the homogenized + water-quenched M2 (M2-HQ) sample
characterization_methods.key_findings: M2-HQ optical micrograph (500 µm scale bar) shows a lighter matrix with scattered dark features.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe-8Mn-3Al-1Si-0.2C (M2) composition; equilibrium phases predicted as a function of temperature; lower critical temperature taken as 600 °C; 1 % Si addition to the 3Al system introduces δ-ferrite in the intercritical temperature range (ICT band ~600-1000 °C).

unmapped_findings: δ-ferrite in M2 steel is stated to form while soaking at 1100 °C before hot rolling (physically the same temperature as the 1100 °C homogenization), and some fraction of α-ferrite forms from γ at finish-rolling temperatures (~900 °C); however, the paper does not explicitly assign δ-ferrite to the M2-HQ (homogenized + water-quenched) state.

No tensile, hardness, or quantitative phase-fraction (XRD/EBSD) measurement is reported specifically for the M2-HQ condition; the mechanical properties and quantitative phase analysis in this paper refer only to the M2-HR (hot-rolled) and M2-IA (intercritically annealed) conditions.
